topic.title: How to Integrate Non-Default Schema Versions for S1000D

body.p: includes built-in support for S1000D 4.x schemas by default. It is possible to integrate other S1000D schema versions (2.x, 3.x, 5.x, 6.x) with some manual configuration.

This best practices guide provides instructions for integrating S1000D 2.x, 3.x, 5.x, and 6.x schemas into , covering both the customization of built-in frameworks as well as methods for creating your own catalogs for maximum flexibility and compatibility.

section.title: Step 1: Download the Required S1000D Schemas
section.p: First, download the official XML schemas directly from s1000d.org. The directory structure varies by version:

li.p: S1000D 6.0: S1000D Issue 6\S1000D Issue 6 XML Schema Package\S1000D 6 XML Schema Package\xml_schema_flat
S1000D 5.0: S1000D Issue 5.0\S1000D Issue 5.0 XML Schema Package\S1000D 5.0 Final - XML Schema Flat and Support Files\xml_schema_flat
S1000D 3.0: S1000D Issue 3.0\XML-SGML Schema-DTD package\S1000D_3-0_xml_schema\S1000D_3-0\xml_schema_flat
S1000D 2.x: S1000D Issue 2.x\XML-SGML Schema-DTD\package\S1000D_2-x_xml_schema\xml_schema

section.p: For legacy data, or certain S1000D 2.x and 3.0 scenarios, you might need to use DTD-based validation.

section.note: Use XML sample files that conform to the DTD structure. Do not use SGML-based files.

section.title: Step 2: Integrate Schemas with Oxygen
section.p: If you have permissions set to alter Oxygen’s built-in frameworks, you can redirect schema resolution for a streamlined editing experience:

li.p: Navigate to the built-in schemas directory: oxygen/frameworks/s1000d_base/schemas.
Create a schema folder per version:

For example, if working with S1000D 5.0 and your XML uses xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="http://www.s1000d.org/S1000D_5-0/xml_schema_flat/comrep.xsd", then create a folder named S1000D_5-0 under schemas/.
Copy your downloaded xml_schema_flat into this directory.
Update the schema catalog:
Open oxygen/frameworks/s1000d_base/catalog.xml.
Add entries to map the online S1000D namespace to your local schema directory:
Repeat for each version as necessary.

p.b: Method B: Creating a Custom XML Catalog

section.p: If modifying internal frameworks is not an option, you can create your own catalog and schemas folder in a writable location:

li.p: Create the directory structure:
Make a folder wherever you have write permissions.
Inside the new folder, create a schemas folder and version-specific subfolders, such as schemas/S1000D_5-0/.
Copy your downloaded xml_schema_flat file into the relevant subfolders.
Create a catalog.xml file:
Add the following content, adjusting versions as needed:
Add entries for each S1000D version needed.
Register the custom catalog in Oxygen:
Go to Options Preferences XML XML Catalog .
Click Add, and enter the path or URL to your custom catalog.xml.

section.title: Step 3: Document Type Association for Legacy Versions
section.p: To integrate older versions (such as S1000D 2.x or 3.x), follow similar steps. However, be aware that the S1000D framework provided by Oxygen may not handle these correctly due to schema syntax differences. Enhanced support is achievable by creating a custom framework with a higher priority than the default, which is typically set to Low.

li.p: Navigate to Options Preferences Document Type Association in Oxygen.
You can extend or duplicate the existing S1000D document type and assign your newly integrated schemas.
Prioritize your custom framework by increasing its priority to ensure it supersedes the default behavior.
